title: Iceland or Tromsø for the northern lights: which is better?
author: Matt
intro: Iceland and Tromsø are the two most popular northern lights trips from the UK, both about three to four hours away. Tromsø sits further north, right under the aurora, and has deep snow and huskies. Iceland is milder, has more direct flights and pairs the lights with waterfalls, glaciers and hot lagoons. Here's how to choose.
seo_title: Iceland or Tromsø for the northern lights?
seo_description: Tromsø is further north, colder and snowier; Iceland is milder, with more flights and more sights. Aurora odds, weather, flights and costs compared.

sections.heading: The short answer
sections.text:
- **Best aurora odds:** Tromsø, just
- **More to see by day:** Iceland
- **Snow and huskies:** Tromsø
- **More direct flights:** Iceland

Both are good places to see the northern lights, and in both the weather matters more than the place: you need dark, clear skies. Pick Tromsø for a proper snowy Arctic winter with sledding and whales. Pick Iceland for road trips, waterfalls, ice caves and geothermal lagoons, with the lights as the evening show.

sections.heading: Side by side
sections.text:
| | [Iceland](/destinations/reykjavik) (Reykjavík) | [Tromsø](/destinations/tromso) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Latitude | about 64°N | about 70°N |
| January high | about 3°C | about -2°C |
| Snow | patchy in Reykjavík | deep and lasting |
| Flight from London | about 3 hrs | about 3½ to 4 hrs |
| Time difference | none | +1 hr |
| Best for | sightseeing, lagoons, road trips | snow, huskies, whales |

The temperatures are average daytime highs from our guides. The aurora season runs from about September to early April in both. Both are expensive, so budget for tours and eating out to cost more than at home.

sections.heading: The northern lights: how they compare
sections.text:
Tromsø sits almost under the auroral oval, the ring around the Arctic where the lights are most often overhead. That gives it a slight edge, and on an active night the lights can fill the whole sky, even from town.

Reykjavík is further south, but still far enough north to see the aurora on most active, clear nights. The city's lights get in the way, so most people take a tour or drive out into the dark. In both places, though, cloud is the real problem, as both are on a stormy Atlantic coast. Tour operators in both chase gaps in the cloud, sometimes driving a long way to find them.

Tip: stay at least three or four nights, and book your northern lights tour for early in the trip. Many operators let you rebook for free if you don't see anything.

sections.heading: Iceland in winter
sections.text:
Iceland is the better choice if you want lots to do by day. From Reykjavík you can easily reach:

- **The Golden Circle:** the Þingvellir rift valley, the Geysir hot springs and the Gullfoss waterfall.
- **The south coast:** the Seljalandsfoss and Skógafoss waterfalls and black-sand beaches, with glacier ice caves further east in winter.
- **Lagoons:** the Blue Lagoon near the airport and the Sky Lagoon near the city, both lovely after dark.

It's milder than Tromsø, often just above freezing in Reykjavík, but very windy, and roads can close in storms. Our [Iceland in 4 days](/blog/iceland-in-4-days) plan has a full itinerary, and the [Iceland Ring Road](/destinations/iceland-ring-road) guide covers a longer trip.

sections.heading: Tromsø in winter
sections.text:
Tromsø is a small, lively Arctic city on an island, ringed by snowy mountains and fjords. It feels like a real winter wonderland, with snow on the ground from about November to April.

- **Husky and reindeer sledding**, often with a Sámi host and a meal round the fire.
- **Whale safaris** into the fjords, which usually run from about November to January.
- **The Fjellheisen cable car**, for views over the city, and the Arctic Cathedral.

Local knowledge: from late November to mid-January Tromsø has the polar night, when the sun doesn't rise. There's still a few hours of blue twilight around midday, but if you want daylight for sledding and photos, go from late January to March. Our guide to the [best time to see the northern lights in Tromsø](/blog/best-time-to-see-the-northern-lights-in-tromso) has more.

sections.heading: Getting there from the UK
sections.text:
- **Iceland:** easyJet, Jet2, Icelandair and British Airways fly to Keflavík from a long list of UK airports, including London, Manchester, Edinburgh and, new this winter with easyJet, Newcastle and Liverpool. The airport is about 45 minutes from Reykjavík.
- **Tromsø:** fewer options. easyJet and Norwegian have flown from Gatwick and Manchester in recent winters, and Norwegian starts flying from Glasgow on 11 December 2026. Some tour operators run winter charter flights too.

Check your airline's schedule for your dates, as both routes are seasonal from some airports. If you can't get a direct flight to Tromsø, it's an easy change in Oslo.

sections.heading: Which should you choose?
sections.text:
- **Choose Tromsø** for the best chance of the lights overhead, deep snow, huskies and whales.
- **Choose Iceland** for more to see by day, lagoons, milder weather and more direct flights.
- **For a first trip with children:** Iceland is gentler, but Tromsø's snow is magical if they can take the cold.
- **For a short break:** Iceland, as there are more flights to fit your dates.

If you're also thinking about Lapland, our [Tromsø or Rovaniemi](/blog/tromso-or-rovaniemi) post compares the two. Can't agree? Add both to somewhere.party, give everyone points to vote with, and let the draw decide.

faqs.question: Is Iceland or Tromsø better for the northern lights?
faqs.answer: Tromsø has a slight edge, because it's further north and almost under the auroral oval. In both places, though, clear skies matter most, so stay several nights to give yourself the best chance.

faqs.question: Is Tromsø colder than Iceland?
faqs.answer: Yes. Tromsø's winter days are usually a few degrees below freezing, with deep snow. Reykjavík is often just above freezing, but very windy.

faqs.question: When is the best time to see the northern lights in Iceland and Tromsø?
faqs.answer: From about September to early April in both. Late January to March is a good balance of dark nights, more daylight and snow.

faqs.question: How long is the flight to Tromsø or Iceland?
faqs.answer: About three hours from London to Reykjavík (Keflavík), and about three and a half to four hours to Tromsø.
